name: Ben Morales
bio: Dentist who wants his retirement savings to grow as fast as possible.
persona: Ben Morales is a 29-year-old dentist at a modern urban clinic. He is single, lives alone, has a high, steady income, almost no debt and about two years of expenses in savings. He wants to invest $97,000 for retirement, roughly 30 years away. Although he knows little about investing and has never been through a market crash, he wants maximum growth and insists losses don't scare him; he says a big drop would just be a chance to buy more. He is warm and evidence-minded at work and wants the same plain explanations about money.

name: Isaac Vargas
bio: Civil engineer saving toward a bigger home.
persona: Isaac Vargas is a 44-year-old civil engineer who works on transportation and land-development projects. He is single and lives alone, has a very stable salary, very little debt and about four months of expenses saved. He wants to invest $78,000 toward a bigger home in about 12 years. He is analytical and methodical, explains things step by step, and is comfortable taking real risk for growth. In a past downturn he held on, and when markets turn rough he stays calm and treats it as a chance to add more. He knows a moderate amount about investing and likes to check the numbers himself.

name: Mina Garcia
bio: Community pharmacist and young parent saving for a house.
persona: Mina Garcia is a 28-year-old pharmacist at a community pharmacy. She is married with one young child, has a very stable income, little debt and about four months of expenses saved. She wants to invest $21,000 for a house down payment in about 10 years. She knows a lot about investing and talks boldly about wanting maximum growth. But she has never watched her own money fall sharply, and when markets turn rough she feels uneasy and would probably trim some holdings rather than buy more. At work she explains things clearly, without jargon.

name: Nadia Zhang
bio: Event bartender with an uneven income, slowly building a safety net.
persona: Nadia Zhang is a 33-year-old event bartender who lives with her partner. Her income rises and falls with event bookings, and student loan and credit card payments take about 41% of it. She has about two months of expenses saved. She wants to put $1,000 toward a house down payment in about 10 years. She is fairly cautious and gets uneasy with big swings; watching her balance shrink makes her anxious, and she tends to cut her losses. She has never invested before and knows little about it. She is warm and funny and likes to say 'another shift, another story'.

name: Sean Gomez
bio: Single dad and marketing coordinator saving for his child's college.
persona: Sean Gomez is a 34-year-old marketing coordinator at a digital marketing agency and a single parent of one young child. His salary is steady, debt payments take about 19% of it, and he has about four months of expenses saved. He wants to invest $12,000 for his child's college in about 10 years. He talks confidently about wanting maximum growth, but he has never been through a market drop with real money, and when markets turn rough he gets uneasy and might trim his holdings. He admits he knows little about investing and uses everyday analogies and self-deprecating humor.

name: Ava Fischer

She knows a lot about money and markets from her work and has never been through a big investment loss, but she is fairly cautious and gets uneasy with big swings; when markets turn rough she would probably trim a little but mostly sit tight. She is warm, practical and asks a lot of questions.

He knows a lot about how investing works and has never been through a big loss, but he avoids risk and would rather earn little than lose anything. If his own money were falling, he would get out fast and lose sleep over it. He is calm, precise and factual.
